blindSummary:
Self-governing in free association with a larger neighbouring state; male same-sex conduct technically criminalised (unenforced, reform pending); population ~1,700; thin data.

The underlying evidence base is that of the associated state, adapted for local conditions.
blindOutOfScope: The record builds on the associated state's evidence base; local deviations noted in summary.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: this public-broadcaster article covers the associated state's police hate-crime data, not this country; included as comparator context for a self-governing state in free association with it.
NOTE: this public-broadcaster article covers a national living-survey of trans and non-binary people in the associated state, not this country; included as comparator context.
International legal-aid trust: overview of criminalising jurisdictions and strategic litigation (bearing on this country: no criminalisation carried over via its association framework).

UN human-rights information sheet (Aug 2015): FAQ on sexual orientation, gender identity and intersex status across the island states of the region - documents this country's indigenous third-gender identity, long established in family and village life, among the region's diverse pre-colonial gender identities, described as an important part of the region's cultural inheritance.

Scholarly book supplement by a historian of ancient law on homosexuality in the law codes of the earliest states (four named ancient codes) - notes they largely ignore homosexual acts; historical context, not specific to this country.

Legal-information site's page on this country's laws: age of majority 21 (men)/19 (women) under a statute dating from 1966; age of consent reportedly equalised in 2011; no recognition of same-sex relationships; HIV testing policy for visitors staying longer than two months.
